quests.instruction: The family is planning a day at the beach. Which preparation is the most useful the evening before?
quests.correctAnswer: Gather Towels, Water and Sun Hats 🏖️
options: Pack Heavy Books and a Laptop 💻
Choose Only the Snacks and Nothing Else 🍪
Gather Towels, Water and Sun Hats 🏖️
quests.hint: Focus on the day itself: sun, sea and time outside.
quests.explanation: A beach day calls for towels, water and hats, and gathering them the evening before avoids a rush. Heavy books or only snacks do not cover what the day needs.
quests.funFact: Beaches can feel much brighter than other places, because sunlight bounces off sand and water.

quests.instruction: The family is visiting a place of worship. Which behaviour shows respect?
quests.correctAnswer: Follow the Customs, Such as Quiet Voices 🤫
options: Follow the Customs, Such as Quiet Voices 🤫
Take Lots of Photos of Everything Inside 📷
Run Around and Play a Game of Tag 🏃
quests.hint: Work out what the people there would expect.
quests.explanation: Different places have their own customs, and following them, like speaking softly, shows respect for people who are praying. Photos or games might disturb them.
quests.funFact: Visitors to some places of worship are asked to remove their shoes or cover their heads, and the customs differ from place to place.

quests.instruction: The family is going to a crowded festival. What should they agree before going in?
quests.correctAnswer: A Meeting Place in Case They Get Separated 📍
options: Who Will Walk the Fastest Through the Fair 🏃
Which Stall Has the Best Snacks 🍬
A Meeting Place in Case They Get Separated 📍
quests.hint: Remember what happens if you lose sight of each other.
quests.explanation: Agreeing on a meeting place beforehand means everyone knows where to go if they get separated. Snacks and speed do not help if someone is lost.
quests.funFact: In a crowd, a fixed landmark such as a gate or a clock tower is easier to find than a person who keeps moving.

quests.instruction: After building a den in the living room, the children have left cushions and blankets everywhere. What should they do?
quests.correctAnswer: Put Everything Back Where It Belongs 🛋️
options: Leave It All for Tomorrow Morning 📅
Put Everything Back Where It Belongs 🛋️
Push It All Into Another Room Nearby 🚪
quests.hint: The clue is who will use the room next.
quests.explanation: Putting cushions and blankets back leaves the room ready for everyone. Leaving it or hiding it in another room just moves the problem.
quests.funFact: Making dens is a popular game around the world, and children have used blankets, branches and boxes for it for generations.

quests.instruction: Zoya has helped make a snack, and there is flour on the counter and a hot pan on the stove. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Wipe the Counter and Leave the Pan Alone 🧽
options: Leave the Whole Mess for Mum to Clear 🙄
Wipe the Counter and Leave the Pan Alone 🧽
Wash the Hot Pan Straight Away Herself 🔥
quests.hint: Think about which part of the clean-up is safe for a child.
quests.explanation: Wiping the counter is safe for a child, but a hot pan should be handled by a grown-up. Washing it straight away could cause burns, and leaving everything would be unfair.
quests.funFact: Metal pans can stay hot for a long time after the heat is turned off.

quests.instruction: After playing in the garden, the football, bat and cones are scattered on the grass, and it looks like rain. What should Hari do?
quests.correctAnswer: Gather Them and Bring Them Inside 🏠
options: Gather Them and Bring Them Inside 🏠
Leave Them Out to Get Wet in the Rain 🌧️
Hide Them in the Long Grass 🌿
quests.hint: Remember what rain does to sports equipment.
quests.explanation: Equipment that is kept dry lasts longer and is ready for next time. Leaving it out or hiding it in the grass risks damage or loss.
quests.funFact: Leather footballs absorb water and become heavy, which is why they are dried and stored indoors.

quests.instruction: Tomorrow is fancy-dress day at school. When should Aanya get her costume ready?
quests.correctAnswer: This Evening, to Find Anything Missing 🎭
options: This Evening, to Find Anything Missing 🎭
In the Morning, After She Wakes Up ⏰
Just Before Class at the School Gate 🚪
quests.hint: Think about when there is still time to fix a problem.
quests.explanation: Getting it ready the evening before leaves time to find a missing piece. Waiting until morning or the school gate is too late for fixes.
quests.funFact: Theatre companies hold dress rehearsals so that costume problems are found before opening night.

quests.instruction: Dev has to leave at five tomorrow morning for a journey. His alarm will ring, but what else will help him wake on time?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask a Grown-up to Wake Him as Well 📞
options: Trust Himself Not to Oversleep Alone 😴
Ask a Grown-up to Wake Him as Well 📞
Stay Up All Night to Be Sure 🌙
quests.hint: Focus on a back-up if one plan fails.
quests.explanation: A second person gives a back-up if the alarm fails or he sleeps through it. Hoping not to oversleep or staying up all night does not help.
quests.funFact: Having a back-up for important wake-ups is common, and many people set two alarms.

quests.instruction: Priya's science project needs glue to dry overnight before school tomorrow. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Finish the Gluing Tonight 🧴
options: Glue It Just Before Showing It 🧪
Glue It on the Bus 🚌
Finish the Gluing Tonight 🧴
quests.hint: Think about how long glue takes to set.
quests.explanation: Glue needs time to set, so finishing tonight means it is dry by morning. Gluing on the bus or just before showing would leave it wet.
quests.funFact: Glue sets by drying or by a chemical change, depending on the type.

quests.instruction: Anu shares a room with her brother, who leaves his clothes on the floor. She is annoyed. What is a good first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Talk Calmly and Agree on Areas for Each 🗣️
options: Talk Calmly and Agree on Areas for Each 🗣️
Throw His Clothes Out of the Bedroom Window 🪟
Tell Mum Every Day to Fix It 📢
quests.hint: Think about a way both of them could be happy.
quests.explanation: Talking calmly and agreeing on areas gives both a say and a fair plan. Throwing things out or relying on Mum to fix it solves nothing.
quests.funFact: A tape line down the middle of a shared room is one way that siblings mark out their own space.

quests.instruction: Two siblings both need the family computer for homework this evening. What is a sensible way to share it?
quests.correctAnswer: Make a Schedule Based on Deadlines 📋
options: Let the Older One Always Win 💪
Make a Schedule Based on Deadlines 📋
Unplug It So Neither Can Use It 🔌
quests.hint: Ask yourself what is fair and practical.
quests.explanation: A schedule by deadline gives priority to whoever needs it most urgently. Letting the older one win or unplugging it is unfair or unhelpful.
quests.funFact: Schools with limited computers often use sign-up sheets so that every child gets time.

quests.instruction: Dev's little sister keeps following him and wants to join his game. What is a kind way to handle it?
quests.correctAnswer: Include Her in a Simple Part of the Game 🤝
options: Include Her in a Simple Part of the Game 🤝
Tell Her Roughly to Go Away and Stay Away 😠
Lock Her Out of the Room Until Later 🔒
quests.hint: Think about how she feels.
quests.explanation: Giving her a simple role includes her and keeps the game going. Locking her out or snapping at her hurts her feelings.
quests.funFact: Younger siblings often learn a lot from watching and playing with older ones.

quests.instruction: On Saturday, Joy wants to play, do her chores, practise piano and visit her grandmother at four. How should she plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Write a List and Place the Fixed Time First 📋
options: Play Until There Is No Time for Anything Else 🎮
Decide Each Thing on the Spot With No Plan 🎲
Write a List and Place the Fixed Time First 📋
quests.hint: Work out which part of the day cannot move.
quests.explanation: The visit at four cannot move, so planning around it makes room for the rest. Playing until nothing fits or deciding on the spot risks missing something.
quests.funFact: An 'agenda' is a list of things to be done, from a Latin word meaning 'things that must be done'.

quests.instruction: A friend cancels, leaving Ravi with a free afternoon. Which is a good way to use it?
quests.correctAnswer: Do Some Homework, Then Choose Something Fun 🎨
options: Sleep Through the Whole Afternoon and Evening 😴
Do Some Homework, Then Choose Something Fun 🎨
Spend the Whole Afternoon on a Screen Alone 📱
quests.hint: Focus on getting the most from the time.
quests.explanation: Doing a bit of homework and then something fun uses the time well. Using it all on a screen or sleeping through it wastes a chance to do both.
quests.funFact: The word 'hobby' once meant a small horse, and later came to mean a favourite pastime.

quests.instruction: It is Sunday evening, and school starts tomorrow. Which job is the most useful before dinner?
quests.correctAnswer: Check Bag, Uniform and Homework 🎒
options: Start a Long New Game on the Tablet 🎮
Plan Next Weekend's Activities 📅
Check Bag, Uniform and Homework 🎒
quests.hint: Work out what tomorrow morning will need.
quests.explanation: A quick check of bag, uniform and homework means Monday morning starts calmly. A long game or planning next weekend does nothing for tomorrow.
quests.funFact: People often call a short Sunday-evening preparation a 'weekly reset'.

quests.instruction: A power cut happens at dinner time and the room goes dark. What is the safest thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Use a Torch and Stay Where You Are 🔦
options: Run to Find a Switch in the Dark 🏃
Light Candles and Carry Them Around 🕯️
Use a Torch and Stay Where You Are 🔦
quests.hint: The key is light that does not need a flame.
quests.explanation: A torch gives safe light, and staying put avoids bumps. Carrying candles can cause fires, and running in the dark can lead to falls.
quests.funFact: Torches run on batteries, so they work when the mains electricity is cut.

quests.instruction: During a long power cut, the fridge has stopped running. What should the family do?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep the Door Closed as Much as Possible 🧊
options: Open It Every Few Minutes to Check the Food 👀
Keep the Door Closed as Much as Possible 🧊
Leave It Wide Open to Cool the Room 🌬️
quests.hint: Think about how to keep the cold in.
quests.explanation: A closed fridge stays cold for hours, which helps keep food safe. Opening it lets cold air escape.
quests.funFact: A closed fridge can keep food cold for around four hours without power.

quests.instruction: It is homework time during a power cut, and the room is dim. What is a sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Go Over Lessons Aloud Until Power Returns 🗣️
options: Go Over Lessons Aloud Until Power Returns 🗣️
Skip It and Tell Nobody Why It Was Missed 🙈
Squint to Try to Write in the Dark Room ✏️
quests.hint: Focus on tasks that do not need strong light.
quests.explanation: Talking through lessons needs no light and keeps her learning. Squinting in the dark strains the eyes, and hiding it from the teacher does not help.
quests.funFact: Reading in dim light does not damage the eyes, but it can make them feel tired.

quests.instruction: Dev has a little pocket money, and a friend's birthday is on Saturday. Which is a sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Choose a Gift Within His Budget 🎁
options: Spend It All on Sweets for Himself 🍬
Choose a Gift Within His Budget 🎁
Borrow Money to Buy an Expensive Gift 💸
quests.hint: Remember what he can afford.
quests.explanation: A gift within his budget is thoughtful and does not cause money trouble. Borrowing or spending everything on himself does not.
quests.funFact: In India, gifts of money are often given as ₹101 or ₹501, because the extra rupee is considered lucky.

quests.instruction: Anu pays for a notebook and is handed some change. What is a sensible habit?
quests.correctAnswer: Count the Change Before Walking Away 💰
options: Give It Back to the Shopkeeper as a Tip 🪙
Put It in Her Pocket Without Looking 🤷
Count the Change Before Walking Away 💰
quests.hint: The key is mistakes that can be fixed quickly.
quests.explanation: Counting at the counter means any mistake can be fixed straight away. Not looking or giving it away makes mistakes harder to correct.
quests.funFact: The Indian rupee symbol, ₹, was adopted in 2010.

quests.instruction: Mina has some money in her bag at school. What is a good way to keep it safe?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep It in a Zipped Pocket or Purse 👛
options: Leave It on Her Desk During Break 🪑
Keep It in a Zipped Pocket or Purse 👛
Show It to Friends to Impress Them 💵
quests.hint: Focus on keeping it hidden and secure.
quests.explanation: A zipped pocket or purse keeps it safe and out of sight. Showing it off or leaving it on a desk makes loss or theft more likely.
quests.funFact: Indian notes differ in size, colour and design so that people can tell them apart.

quests.instruction: Dev's tablet is on his bed at night. What is the best routine?
quests.correctAnswer: Charge It Outside the Bedroom 🔌
options: Charge It Outside the Bedroom 🔌
Watch One Last Video in Bed 📱
Sleep with It Under the Pillow 🛏️
quests.hint: Focus on sleep and screens.
quests.explanation: Charging it outside the bedroom removes the temptation to use it and helps sleep. A device under the pillow or a last video keeps the mind alert.
quests.funFact: Notifications and bright screens can wake people up or make it harder to fall asleep.

quests.instruction: Zoya is doing homework on the computer, and a game is open in another tab. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Close the Game Until Homework Is Done 💻
options: Keep the Game Open in a Small Window 🪟
Play a Round Between Every Question 🎮
Close the Game Until Homework Is Done 💻
quests.hint: Ask yourself what pulls her attention away.
quests.explanation: Closing the game removes the distraction. Keeping it open, even small, makes it easy to drift away from the homework.
quests.funFact: Switching attention between tasks can take extra time and effort.

quests.instruction: Mina wants to share a photo of her friends online. What should she do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask Her Friends and a Grown-up First 📷
options: Post It Right Away 📤
Ask Her Friends and a Grown-up First 📷
Change Their Faces to Look Silly and Post It 🤪
quests.hint: Ask yourself who the photo belongs to.
quests.explanation: Friends have a say about photos of them, and a grown-up can help with online safety. Posting at once or changing faces without asking could upset people.
quests.funFact: Once a photo is online, it can be copied and shared, which is why people check first.

quests.instruction: After finishing a juice bottle, what is the best thing to do with it at home?
quests.correctAnswer: Rinse It and Put It in the Recycling 🍾
options: Rinse It and Put It in the Recycling 🍾
Put It in with the Wet Food Waste 🍌
Leave It Beside the Road for Others 🛣️
quests.hint: Work out how glass or plastic can be used again.
quests.explanation: A rinsed bottle can be recycled and made into new things. Food waste or roadside litter does not.
quests.funFact: Glass can be recycled many times without losing quality.

quests.instruction: Hari is brushing his teeth. Which habit saves water?
quests.correctAnswer: Turn the Tap Off While Brushing 🚰
options: Turn the Tap Off While Brushing 🚰
Leave It Running the Whole Time 💧
Fill the Sink and Leave It Overnight 🪣
quests.hint: Remember when the water is actually needed.
quests.explanation: Turning the tap off while brushing saves litres of water that would otherwise go down the drain.
quests.funFact: A running tap can use several litres of water every minute.

quests.instruction: Leo has a sheet of paper that is printed on one side. What is a good use for the other side?
quests.correctAnswer: Use It for Rough Work or Drawing 📄
options: Throw It Away Straight Away Today 🗑️
Burn It in the Garden 🔥
Use It for Rough Work or Drawing 📄
quests.hint: The key is getting more use out of it.
quests.explanation: The blank side is still useful for rough work, which saves paper. Throwing it away wastes it, and burning paper is unsafe and pollutes the air.
quests.funFact: Making paper uses a lot of water and energy, so reusing it helps.

quests.instruction: The family plans a day trip tomorrow, and rain is forecast for the afternoon. What is the best thing to do tonight?
quests.correctAnswer: Pack Rain Gear, Water and Snacks 🎒
options: Plan to Pack in the Car on the Way 🚗
Pack Rain Gear, Water and Snacks 🎒
Pack Only Swimming Things 🏊
quests.hint: Work out what the weather and the long day each need.
quests.explanation: Rain gear, water and snacks cover the forecast and the long day. Swimming things do not suit rain, and packing in the car invites forgotten items.
quests.funFact: A 'mackintosh' raincoat is named after Charles Macintosh, who patented waterproof rubberised cloth in the 1820s.

quests.instruction: Which describes a good family routine for the end of a busy day?
quests.correctAnswer: A Short, Calm Wind-down Everyone Can Follow 🌙
options: No Routine at All 🚫
A Long, Complicated Plan That Changes Daily 🔄
A Short, Calm Wind-down Everyone Can Follow 🌙
quests.hint: Work out what people actually keep doing when they are tired.
quests.explanation: A short, calm routine is easy to keep up, even on tired days. Complicated plans and no plan are harder to follow.
quests.funFact: Aeroplane safety cards use pictures and few words so that everyone can follow them quickly.

quests.instruction: Which is the best way to learn from a day that went badly?
quests.correctAnswer: Think Back and Try One Small Change 🔧
options: Think Back and Try One Small Change 🔧
Blame Everyone Else for What Went Wrong 👈
Decide That Nothing Can Ever Be Changed 🏳️
quests.hint: Remember what helps people do better next time.
quests.explanation: Looking at what happened and changing one thing gives a better chance next time. Blaming others or giving up changes nothing.
quests.funFact: Writing down one thing that went well and one thing to change takes only a minute.
